key_insight: An algorithmic stability framework bounds expected catastrophic forgetting under SGD by linking sample-perturbation propagation, learning-rate schedules, and cumulative gradient alignment.
engineering_relevance: The bounds help engineers reason about how dataset size, updates per task, task count, and learning-rate decay restarts influence forgetting in continual learning.
method: Decompose forgetting into intra-task and cross-task generalization gaps plus empirical forgetting.
Track sample perturbations across SGD updates under constant, intra-task decaying, and continuously decaying learning rates.
Bound empirical forgetting using cumulative gradient alignment without requiring convexity.
evidence_signal: Experiments on Split CIFAR-100 and Split MiniImageNet examine empirical implications of the theory; the abstract reports no quantitative results.
watch_item: The results bound expected forgetting under SGD, so their tightness and usefulness for other optimizers require validation.
paper_title: Fine-Grained Analysis of Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Learning via Algorithmic Stability
